normGaps.detail: No norm defines folding one repository into another. A fold is modeled as the act the norms do define: the TOC Archived stage on supersession (toc/README.md, TOC vote, simple majority), taken after the host imports the content, with context kept in the README (GOVERNANCE.md 11).

toc/README.md names "Sustained inactivity, maintainer request, or supersession" and GOVERNANCE.md 11 says "Archive only when inactive or superseded, and keep context in README.", but no norm says how long inactivity must last; a quiet window only raises a candidate.

toc/README.md specifies how to apply for Sandbox, Incubation and Graduation, but not how an archival is proposed, by whom, or the title it is filed under; the staged application uses "[Archived] <repository>" by analogy with "[Incubation]" and "[Graduation]".

STANDARDS.md status tags [active, maintenance, deprecated, archived] include [deprecated], which neither the TOC stages [Sandbox, Incubation, Graduated, Archived] nor the GOVERNANCE.md 11 lifecycle [Proposal, Active, Maintenance, Archived] defines, so a deprecation has no lifecycle decision.

No norm says what happens to the open issues and pull requests of a repository that is archived or folded; the staged acts transfer open issues to the host, which GitHub allows only within one organization.
